- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for downward bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a 2–5% downward correction.  
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 18-day average (e.g., < 90% of mean), consider mean reversion bias — adjust upward by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or positive.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often lags by 1–2 periods; if sentiment is trending upward, anticipate a 1–2 day delay in price recovery — adjust forecast to reflect that lag.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33–1.00), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecasts by averaging last 3–5 periods unless sentiment strongly signals reversal.
